New regression test never asserts the non-object-damaged file's own name appears in stderr

Non-object JSON line drops the whole transcript file instead of skipping just that entry, deviating from the PRD ("skip non-object transcript entries" and keep processing the rest of that file); the agoge branch's converted regression fails against HEAD (expects slices_kept=2, got 1)

The implementer's own new test pins the whole-file-drop deviation: m_non_object.jsonl holds a valid secret-bearing dict line that is asserted NOT to count, when the PRD's per-line-skip reading would count it

PRD explicitly asks to convert the agoge branch's xfail regressions to normal tests when present; neither of the two was ported, and the combined test cannot exercise the encoding regression independently since it dies on the non-object file first

The non-object-damage warning path is unpinned: only the non-UTF-8 file's name is asserted in stderr, not the non-object file's name or line number, though the PRD requires warnings to identify affected paths

Decode isolation is per-8KB-read-buffer, not per-file: entries before a bad byte within the same buffer are still lost, and the stderr warning falsely claims the whole file was skipped (probe: 2000-line file with one bad byte near the end counted only 1917)
Stderr warnings print path.name only, not the full path, making it harder for an operator to locate the damaged transcript under its per-project hash directory
Test prose slop: docstring/comment inaccuracies (wrong file position described, wrong content description) and a stdout anti-leak assertion that can never fail in a dry run
Ordinary-root CLI regression cannot fail (HOME isolation mismatch between test process and subprocess)
Unrequested production change: project_memory_dir special-cased .claude-basename roots
Rework's HOME isolation does not isolate Path.home() on Windows (USERPROFILE vs HOME); repo's isolate_home fixture exists and was not used
